description: LLM-powered multiagent persona simulation for imagination enhancement and business insights.

summary.one_liner: TinyTroupe is an experimental Python library from Microsoft that simulates multiple LLM-driven personas (TinyPersons) interacting in simulated environments (TinyWorlds) for market research, ads testing, and business insight.
summary.what_it_does: The library defines agents (TinyPerson) with detailed personas covering traits, preferences, beliefs, and behaviors, loadable from JSON or built programmatically. Agents receive stimuli through listen/see methods and act through act, and TinyWorld environments run them step by step, with agents in each step running in parallel. TinyPersonFactory generates diverse populations from demographic specs using LLMs and sampling plans. The README also describes empirical validation against real survey data using t-test and KS-test, LLM API and simulation-state caching, cost tracking, and action quality checks. A Jupyter widget supports interactive chat with agents.
use_cases: simulate focus groups for product feedback
evaluate ad options with a simulated audience
test chatbots or copilots with simulated user input
validate simulated survey results against real data
get persona-based feedback on project proposals
how_to_run: Set OPENAI_API_KEY (or AZURE_OPENAI_KEY and AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT) environment variables
jupyter notebook  (then open the examples/ folder)
notable: Persona agents (TinyPerson) with JSON specs, fragments for reusable persona parts, and a population factory driven by demographic files
Empirical validation class comparing simulated results with real survey data via statistical tests
Action quality control that checks agent outputs against persona specs and can regenerate them
Explicitly positioned as a simulator of people rather than an assistant, with Jupyter-notebook-centered workflow
Built-in caching of LLM calls and simulation state to reduce API cost
caveats: Explicitly a work-in-progress research project; the API changes frequently and past releases broke existing programs
Requires paid access to OpenAI or Azure OpenAI APIs; local Ollama support is described as experimental and limited
The README says the library is meant for research and simulation only and carries a legal disclaimer on responsibility for outputs
